findings.topic: Transaction shape (market read + append in ONE prepared transaction)
findings.verdict: CORRECT - proven by construction, not by the new rows
evidence: src/lib/events/journal/SQLiteEventJournalWriter.ts:112-136 - `return this.db .transaction(() => { const prepared = prepare(this.db); ... const result = extend(this.db, prepared.context, () => this.appendInTransaction(...)); ... }) .immediate();`. `prepare` is invoked at :114, INSIDE the transaction body, and `.immediate()` at :136 makes BEGIN IMMEDIATE take the write lock before the callback runs. The read and the append are therefore structurally one immediate write transaction; there is no code path in which prepare runs outside it.

src/lib/campaign/authority/campaignAcceptContractCommand.ts:229-234 - the call site passes the market read as the prepare callback: `return prepared.appendPreparedWithExtension<...>((db) => { const source = readCampaignSourceMarket(db, request.campaignId); ... }`.

src/lib/campaign/authority/campaignAcceptContractCommand.ts:138-160 - `readCampaignSourceMarket(db, campaignId)` takes the BORROWED handle, issues exactly one `SELECT version, payload FROM campaigns WHERE id = ?`, is synchronous, retains no statement and performs no write. It satisfies the prepared-transaction contract stated at SQLiteEventJournalWriter.ts:88-97 ('`prepare` is contractually read-only ... MUST finish synchronously ... no await, returned thenables, timers, microtasks').
No second read exists outside the transaction: `readCampaignSourceMarket` has exactly one call site, and it is inside `prepare`.
findings.staleReadNote: `priorEvents` (campaignCommandPipeline.ts:379) IS read outside the transaction and is used inside prepare for `priorEvents.length` (the sequence base, the expectedRevision via toJournalBatch, and the digest fold). That is SAFE and not a defect: `appendInTransaction` re-reads the stream head inside the transaction and returns `revision-conflict` on mismatch (SQLiteEventJournalWriter.ts:178-190), which campaignAcceptContractCommand.ts:317-320 maps to the typed `lostRaceConflict`. A command racing another commit is refused, never committed on a stale base. This is the same shape the pre-existing non-accept path already had.

busyHandling.question: Is SQLITE_BUSY a typed refusal or a crash?
busyHandling.answer: A CRASH, not a typed refusal - but pre-existing and not a regression.
busyHandling.chain: A BUSY that outlasts the busy timeout is thrown by better-sqlite3 out of `.immediate()`, propagates unchanged out of `appendPreparedWithExtension` (SQLiteEventJournalWriter.ts:97 documents 'Thrown failures propagate unchanged'), out of `appendDurableAcceptContract` (no try/catch anywhere in campaignAcceptContractCommand.ts), out of `executeCampaignCommand`, and lands in the route's catch at src/pages/api/campaigns/[id]/commands.ts:232-234 -> `sendCaughtApiError` -> src/pages-modules/api/routeHelpers.ts:96-102 `res.status(500).json({ error: apiErrorMessage(error, fallback) })` with :20-22 `return error instanceof Error ? error.message : fallback` - i.e. an untyped 500 echoing the raw SQLite message.
busyHandling.notARegression: The pre-existing non-accept path also runs `.immediate()` (SQLiteEventJournalWriter.ts:74-80, reached via `append`/`appendWithExtension`), so BUSY already surfaced the same way before this change. The stack introduces no new BUSY-to-crash surface, only a longer critical section (see R4).

busyTimeoutRR1.measured: Absent as an EXPLICIT pragma - src/services/persistence/SQLiteService.ts:79-86 sets only `journal_mode = WAL` and `foreign_keys = ON`, with `new Database(this.config.path)` at :79 taking no options. But better-sqlite3 applies its own default: measured in-session against this worktree's better-sqlite3 12.11.1, `new Database(f).pragma('busy_timeout')` returns `[{"timeout":5000}]`. The effective busy timeout is 5000 ms, not 0.
busyTimeoutRR1.correction: RR-1 is accurate about the missing explicit pragma and inaccurate if read as 'the connection fails BUSY immediately'. The 5 s C-level default stands.
busyTimeoutRR1.practicalScope: Contention needs TWO connections to the same file. `getSQLiteService()` is a process singleton handing out ONE `Database` handle (SQLiteService.ts:91-98), and better-sqlite3 is synchronous, so within one Node process every writer already serializes on the thread and can never contend. The test's rival is a SEPARATE `new Database(databasePath)` (campaignCommandPipelineOfferDurability.test.ts:345), which production does not have. BUSY is therefore reachable only across processes (a second host on the same file), which is not a configuration this app ships today.

findings.topic: Offer source (persisted campaigns row, never the private baseline; caller body never trusted)
evidence: campaignAcceptContractCommand.ts:142-147 - the read is `SELECT version, payload FROM campaigns WHERE id = ?`, i.e. the persisted `SerializedCampaign` record, exactly what D13 specifies (design.md:133: 'The read is of the source body taken under the command's OWN prepared transaction, never of a previously-stored private baseline').

campaignAcceptContractCommand.ts:132-136 - the module's own comment states the reason and is accurate: `replayCampaignSourceContracts` refuses with `no-private-payload` on a stream with no prior private row, so a stored-baseline read would deadlock every first acceptance.

The first-acceptance row PINS this rather than asserting it: __tests__/campaignCommandPipelineOfferDurability.test.ts:233-242 reads the pre-command stream and asserts `replayCampaignSourceContracts(before)` THROWS `CampaignSourcePrivateReplayError`, then :244-247 asserts the command commits anyway. That is the non-tautological form - a stored-baseline implementation fails this row.

Server-derivation: campaignAcceptContractCommand.ts:250-255 builds the validated payload as `{ contractId: offer.id, name: offer.name, employerFactionId: offer.employerId }` - the exact opaque `IContract.employerId`, no alias table, no case folding, satisfying the spec wording.

Caller-divergence is ASSERTED, not assumed: the intent fixture at test:96-104 deliberately carries `name: 'CALLER SUPPLIED NAME'` and `employerFactionId: 'caller-supplied-employer'`, and test:251-257 asserts the committed payload is `{contractId: STORED_ID, name: stored.name, employerFactionId: stored.employerId}`. The same assertion is repeated on the rollback retry (test:334-340) and the rival row (test:402-408). A caller-derived implementation fails all three; red-62a.log shows exactly that failure at base.
findings.callerObjectUse: The caller's `contract` object is used for exactly two things, both correct: (a) the artifact-use consult's artifactId (campaignCommandPipeline.ts:414-421) - pre-existing and unchanged, and it is the id BEING REQUESTED; (b) the lookup key `intent.payload.contract.contractId` (campaignAcceptContractCommand.ts:220) and the echo in the refusal body. Nothing else on the caller object reaches the commit.
findings.provenanceCaveat: The gate proves DURABILITY, not PROVENANCE. `PUT /api/campaigns/[id]` explicitly 'trusts the caller for the deep envelope shape' (src/pages/api/campaigns/[id].ts:92-93 comment; the guard at :104-112 checks only campaignId / schemaVersion / body-is-object) and carries NO authentication at all (admission brief OB-2, independently re-read this session). So a caller can PUT a fabricated `contractMarket` and then have the server 'derive' that fabrication back. This is not a defect of the change - it is exactly the property D13 admits ('Contract-market offers are ALREADY source-record facts', design.md:127) - and the module comment at campaignAcceptContractCommand.ts:209-211 ('Deriving the committed name or employer from it would let a browser mint a contract the source never stored') stays literally true, since a PUT-then-accept IS a contract the source stored. Recorded so no later reader over-reads 'server-derived' as 'server-minted'.

findings.topic: Privacy - full contract + reduced market private-only, envelopeOf still the single narrowing, 409 body clean
findings.verdict: CORRECT - nothing new on the wire
evidence: campaignAcceptContractCommand.ts:293-312 - the full `IContract` and the reduced market go to `toJournalBatch({... sourcePrivate: buildCampaignSourcePrivateEnvelope({...})})`; `toJournalBatch` (JournalCampaignEventStore.ts:198-232) rides `sourcePrivate` on the terminal event's envelope, and JournalCampaignEventStore.ts:99 states 'so `envelopeOf` cannot carry it to any wire read path'.

The public compact fact contains only the three-field contract (campaignAcceptContractCommand.ts:250-255 -> validateCampaignIntent -> `mk('ContractAccepted', { contract })` at CampaignMatchHostIntent.ts:197-200). No payment terms, no salvage rights, no target, no market.
Pinned by the suite: test:288-292 asserts `campaignSourcePrivateOf(terminal)` is non-null AND `JSON.stringify(terminal.payload.campaignEvent)` does not contain 'paymentTerms'.

envelopeOf narrowing is UNCHANGED and not bypassed: the only non-test `envelopeOf` call sites are projectCampaignStreamForGrant.ts:259, campaignJournalReads.ts:41 and :63, JournalCampaignEventStore.ts:296 and :423, and GmCampaignImpactDerivation.ts:157 - none of which this stack touches. The acknowledgement path goes THROUGH it: campaignCommandPipeline.ts:316-331 `acknowledgeCommit` calls `store.getEvents`, which maps `envelopeOf` at JournalCampaignEventStore.ts:296 / :423.
The `committed` HTTP body (commands.ts:151-156) returns `result.events` (the compact events) and `result.state` (the compact `ICampaignAuthoritativeState`). No private field can reach it.

The new 409 body (commands.ts:208-217) is `{kind: 'offer-not-durable', contractId, reason}` - `contractId` is the caller's own id echoed back and `reason` is a closed 3-value enum. It leaks nothing the caller did not send.
unchangedResiduals: OB-1 (ViewerProjectionService.ts:265-269 bypasses envelopeOf): untouched, still not registered for CAMPAIGN_STREAM_TYPE, and the prefix-3 doc comment does not change it.

OB-2 (unauthenticated `GET /api/campaigns/:id` returns the full `SerializedCampaign` including `contractMarket` with every full `IContract`): untouched by this stack and already owned by the separately-scoped route-auth-guard work. Worth noting for the program owner that after 6.2a the SAME bytes the private envelope protects are the bytes that route already serves unauthenticated - so the privacy win here is real on the journal wire and bounded by OB-2 on the HTTP CRUD surface.

findings.topic: Refusal kind distinctness, sub-reason correctness, uniform fail-closed on in-memory journals
evidence: campaignCommandPipeline.ts:153-168 - `offer-not-durable` is a KIND of its own on `CampaignCommandResult`, not another `rejected` reason string, with a comment giving the exact operational reason ('A caller that could not tell this apart from `insufficient-standing` would give up on the one that a retry fixes'). This satisfies tasks.md 6.2a's 'a typed reason DISTINCT from every rules refusal' and spec.md:203.

Sub-reasons map correctly: `source-read-unavailable` when the journal exposes no prepared transaction (campaignAcceptContractCommand.ts:226-227); `source-record-absent` when the read returns null - no campaigns row, no `body`, or no rehydratable `contractMarket` (:234-237 with :147 / :152 / :154); `offer-absent` when the market exists and lacks the id (:238-242).
Fail-closed is uniform and there is NO fallback branch to the caller's contract anywhere in the module - verified by reading all 341 lines.
Exhaustiveness at the route is real: commands.ts:226-230 keeps `const exhaustive: never = result;`, so adding the kind without the 409 case would have been a tsc error, not a silent 500.

findings.topic: Tests - red logs, non-tautology, the SqliteError workaround
findings.verdict: SOUND, with two rows weaker than their names

rowByRow.assessment: STRONG. Asserts the exact result object, an unchanged journal length, AND no receipt for the commandId. Red-proven.
GOOD. Red-proven, exact result object, no receipt. Weaker than row 1 only in that it does not also pin journal length; with no campaigns row and no receipt this is adequate.

rowByRow.row: first acceptance, no prior private row (test:223-293)
rowByRow.assessment: STRONGEST ROW IN THE STACK. Pins the pre-command `no-private-payload` throw (so a stored-baseline implementation fails it), the server-derived compact fact against a deliberately divergent caller body, a COLD REOPEN of the temp DB before reading the private facts back (so durability is proven, not in-process state), the captured `sourceRecordBody` round-tripping to the seeded body byte-for-byte, `sourceRowVersion === 7`, the reduced market missing exactly the accepted offer, `declinedOfferIds` preserved, and the wire payload free of 'paymentTerms'.

STRONG for ATOMICITY - unchanged journal length, no receipt, unchanged high-water, and a retry that re-derives from the stored offer. It does NOT discriminate read-inside-transaction from read-immediately-before-BEGIN; it proves the append is atomic with whatever prepare produced.

WEAKER THAN ITS NAME. The rival writes from inside a trigger on the `event_journal_events` INSERT, i.e. from inside OUR transaction's critical section. It would therefore get SQLITE_BUSY even if the market read had happened just BEFORE `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, and the committed fact would still name 'house-davion' because the rival never commits in either case. So the row proves 'the append holds a write lock and a rival cannot interleave with it' - not 'the read and the append are one transaction'. Its red at base (red-62a.log) is the caller-supplied-fact mismatch, not a transaction-window failure, which confirms the row never discriminated on the window. The window property IS established, but by construction at SQLiteEventJournalWriter.ts:112-136, not by this row; the row's own comment at test:395-398 cites that mechanism correctly, so the calibration gap is in the row TITLE and in the author's redFirst row-5 claim, not in the code.

sqliteErrorWorkaround.reasoning: The row captures the rejection via `.then(() => null, (error) => error)` (test:315-318) and then asserts `(failure)?.name === 'SqliteError'` plus `String(failure)` containing the injected message (test:319-320). Both are realm-independent, which is the correct response to the documented cross-realm `instanceof Error` failure. Critically it is NOT tautological: if the implementation did not throw, `failure` is `null`, `?.name` is `undefined`, and the row fails. The only theoretical hole - a non-Error object carrying `name: 'SqliteError'` - is unreachable here.
sqliteErrorWorkaround.durability: The underlying tool finding (native-module errors failing `instanceof Error` under jest depending on which suites shared the module registry) is a genuine, durable, cross-project gotcha and is correctly recorded as `durable: true` in the author evidence.
sqliteErrorWorkaround.flakeProbe: Re-ran the new suite standalone 3x and the authority+journal set with `--runInBand` (40 suites / 363 tests) at the tip. No ordering flake reproduced; the workaround holds in both modes.

Re-splitting now would discard three already-green per-prefix gate runs and re-open the byte-identity evidence for a 10-line cap correction on the insertions+deletions reading (461 insertions is already inside the cap on the insertions reading). carryForward.finding: campaignAcceptContractCommand.ts:119-121 documents `null` as covering 'no row, an unreadable body, or a body with no `contractMarket`'. The code does not cover an unreadable body: :148 `JSON.parse(row.payload)` THROWS a SyntaxError on a malformed payload, and :153 `rehydrateContractMarket(body.contractMarket)` reaches `market.offers.map(...)` (missionSerialization.ts:74) which throws a TypeError when `contractMarket` is present but malformed (e.g. `{}`). Only `body === undefined` and `market === undefined` return null. Both throws are reachable: `PUT /api/campaigns/[id]` does not validate the deep envelope shape (src/pages/api/campaigns/[id].ts:92-93, guard at :104-112) and carries no authentication.

The cost is an untyped 500 echoing the raw parser message instead of the typed `source-record-absent` the taxonomy promises.

carryForward.recommendation: Keep the row - it is genuine regression cover for 'a rival cannot interleave with the append' and a useful pin on `.immediate()` semantics. Correct the TITLE and the evidence claim to what it proves ('a concurrent writer is serialized against the committed append'), and let the window property rest where it actually lives: `prepare` is invoked inside the transaction body at SQLiteEventJournalWriter.ts:114, which the row's own comment at test:395-398 already cites.

carryForward.finding: The change materially LENGTHENS the write-lock critical section for an acceptance. Before, only the append ran inside `.immediate()`; now the campaigns-row SELECT, the `JSON.parse`, the market rehydration, `validateCampaignIntent`, the event sequencing, a full `replayCampaignEvents` fold over the whole prior stream and `computeCampaignStateDigest` all run inside it (campaignAcceptContractCommand.ts:233-313). The replay is O(stream length) and grows with campaign age.
carryForward.whyItIsNotAFindingAgainstThisStack: Within a single Node process there is exactly one `Database` handle (SQLiteService.ts:91-98) and better-sqlite3 is synchronous, so writers already serialize on the thread and the longer section costs latency, not contention. Cross-process contention needs a second host on the same file, which is not a shipped configuration, and there is no production caller of AcceptContract through this route yet (`CAMPAIGN_JOURNAL_AUTHORITY_ENABLED` stays false; contract-market.tsx handleAccept is unchanged).
